title: A pro-isomorphism of inverse systems in a triangulated category induces an isomorphism of their derived limits
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a triangulated category D and inverse systems (K_n) and (M_n) in D with derived limits K and M, and asserts that a pro-isomorphism a : (K_n) -> (M_n) of pro-objects can be used to produce a non-canonical isomorphism K -> M (source lines 23169-23176). The proof must extract information from a morphism of pro-systems that is only invertible in the pro-category, where the passage to the limit is not functorial in the naive sense; the argument produces the isomorphism by choosing the comparison maps at large enough indices and combining them with the structural maps of the two derived limits, so that the resulting composite is an isomorphism even though no single index-by-index map witnesses it. The author records explicitly that the isomorphism is non-canonical. The proof is contained in the counted proof span and is the author's own.
